messages:
maria: Quick ping — PR #5678 (kv-cache: avoid double-evict) is ready for review. Tests pass locally but CI keeps failing an intermittent e2e: `test_kv_eviction`. Can someone triage?

jonathan: I glanced at the CI run. The runner shows an allocation spike then this in the logs: 
```
ERROR: RuntimeError: KV eviction failed: attempt to read freed entry
  File "tests/e2e/test_kv_eviction.py", line 78, in test_evict
    assert cache.get(k) is not None
RuntimeError: invalid memory access
```

ci-bot: buildkite/pr-5678 — failed (job #325) — see details: https://ci.example.com/builds/325 :warning:

maria: repro steps i used: `./scripts/run_e2e.sh --seed 42 --repeat 20` — fails ~1/8 runs. I haven't been able to reproduce on my dev GPU consistently. Added more logging locally and pushed branch `pr/5678-debug-logs`.

sam: I can try to repro on my workstation (PST) in a loop. If it's timing/race-related maybe we need a stress harness.

lisa: Quick thought — PR changes eviction ordering and touches async batch flush. Could be a race where a KV entry is evicted while an in-flight request is still referencing it. Try adding a short barrier or bump the refcount path to see if the failure rate drops.

jonathan: Good call. I'll run the e2e in a tight loop in a container to catch it: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do ./scripts/run_e2e.sh --seed $RANDOM || break; done
```
I'll also attach gdb if it breaks.

maria: pushed debug logging and a temporary `atomic_refcount` patch to `pr/5678-debug-logs` to force the safer path. CI queued a rerun.

ci-bot: buildkite/pr-5678 — rerun requested by maria — queued (job #326) :white_check_mark:

sam: If this blocks other merges we should add a hold label and a short note in the PR so infra doesn't auto-merge other dependent branches.

maria: added `hold-merge` label and left a comment on the PR. Thanks. @jonathan @sam please post any reproductions or stack traces here.

lisa: :thumbsup: I can also try a quick local run on a machine with similar CUDA/drivers to the CI runner.

jonathan: reproduced locally after ~45 iterations — attaching clipped trace: 
```
Thread 1 "pytest" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
0x00007f9b3a1b2c3d in kv_entry_free ()
#0  kv_entry_free () at src/kv.c:412
#1  0x00007f9b3a1b3f10 in eviction_worker () at src/evict.c:128
#2  0x00007f9b3a1b4a90 in thread_start (arg=0x7f9b3c000) at src/threads.c:56
```

maria: thanks — that stack points to the exact spot i changed. i'll push a quick fix that adds an explicit acquire before eviction and re-run CI.

sam: sounds good. If the quick-fix reduces flakiness we can follow-up with a proper refactor. For blocking: i'm available in ~2 hours to help.

maria: pushed `pr/5678-fix-evict-acquire` — buildkite job queued. Also left a note `EXPERIMENTAL: added acquire to eviction path` in PR description.

ci-bot: buildkite/pr-5678 — job #327 started — running tests

lisa: :eyes: will monitor. If green for 3 consecutive runs we can remove hold-merge and merge.

jonathan: thanks all. small ask — when you ping for flaky CI please mention if it's blocking a release or other PRs, helps prioritize.

maria: noted — this is blocking the release branch cut for tomorrow so high priority. Thanks everyone. :pray:
